hierarchy.original_event: A rubber ball is dropped onto a hard floor.
hierarchy.regime_criterion:
Define action boundaries by CONTACT MODE and GOVERNING CONDITIONS,
not by whether an object's movement is continuous. One atomic physical regime has
the same kind of contact constraint and driving mechanism throughout. Separate
flight without contact, a transient impact, and sustained surface contact when the
description includes those transitions. Also separate a change of contact mode or
an explicitly changed driving mechanism. A continuous trajectory can cross several
regimes, and using the same object does not make them one action.
An external force/drive being applied or removed IS a governing-condition change,
even if contact mode stays the same. Driven motion and passive coasting are separate.
Within unchanged contact/driving conditions, gradual changes of speed, frequency,
amplitude, orientation or direction do not alone require another action. Deceleration
to rest under unchanged conditions MUST remain in that same action, not a separate
slowing/stopping child. Rest does not add vibration.
Preserve coupled simultaneous behavior within one regime. Do not invent transitions
or split into microscopic mechanics. Model availability does not determine atomicity.
A scenario model that explicitly covers all regime transitions may still handle the
whole action as one MODEL-COVERED leaf; this does not claim the action is atomic.

catalog.name: vertical_bounce
catalog.applicability: Passive vertical drop/rebound process on a fixed flat surface, with one or more contacts. Point-body approximation without spin. Not active dribbling or later rolling.

catalog.name: free_fall
catalog.applicability: Free vertical flight ending at first surface contact. No impact vibration is generated by this model; split off a subsequent impact when needed.

catalog.name: single_impact
catalog.applicability: One isolated normal impact against a fixed surface. Does not include repeated action or a separately described ringing tail.

catalog.name: sliding
catalog.applicability: Sliding/dragging on a flat horizontal surface with Coulomb friction, either unpowered coasting or externally maintained constant speed. Not rolling, curved/inclined surfaces or arbitrary varying force.

catalog.name: rolling
catalog.applicability: Rolling on a flat horizontal surface with effective constant rolling-resistance deceleration. Curved/inclined surfaces are unsupported. No bounce-to-roll conversion is inferred.

catalog.name: damped_oscillation
catalog.applicability: One decaying ringing/vibration tail after excitation. The excitation impact itself must be separate if also requested.

catalog.name: periodic
catalog.applicability: Continuous steady periodic vibration of a motor/tool. Uses a sinusoidal carrier. Not a small count of distinct knocks.

catalog.name: stochastic
catalog.applicability: Irregular independent contacts such as sparse raindrops/gravel, represented by a Poisson process or its fixed-count conditional form.

catalog.name: rhythmic_action
catalog.applicability: Intentional repeated knocks/steps/taps, including active dribbling. Cadence is behavioral, not passive restitution.

equations: count = number of contacts with e^(k-1) >= 0.1

height_m.basis: typical drop height for a rubber ball from hand level in everyday scenarios

restitution.basis: material properties of rubber and energy retention during impact with hard surfaces

mass_kg.basis: typical mass of a standard-sized rubber ball (e.g., tennis or soccer ball size)

notes: Assumed constant restitution, a rigid stationary floor, no drag and instantaneous contact.
Material names describe the impact caption; they do not determine a calibrated restitution coefficient.
Pulse duration is a rendering choice, not predicted physical contact time.
Intensity is normalized impulse, not measured acceleration or perceived strength.
The requested/rendered contact count is not a prediction of when the ball stops.
Some rendering pulses overlap; physical impact times were preserved without stretching.
Contact count derived from restitution: contacts below 10% of the first impulse are treated as stopped.
Omitted contacts not rendered (render limit of 8 events): 1.
Rendering windows overlap; physical event times are not stretched apart.
Source/parameter extraction is an LM judgment. Defaults are unmeasured assumptions.
LM estimates (if any) are plausibility judgments with stated ranges, not measurements.
Normalized amplitude is not calibrated perceived strength or cross-model force.
